sources.title: Microsoft Learn: Common web application architectures

claims.text: Microsoft describes managing application complexity by dividing code by responsibilities or concerns, restricting inter-layer communication for encapsulation, and limiting the impact of replacing a layer to collaborating layers.

Microsoft documents traditional top-to-bottom compile-time dependencies (UI to BLL to DAL), the resulting business-logic dependency on data-access details and testing difficulty, and describes dependency inversion with infrastructure depending on application-core abstractions.

Microsoft documents that even a single deployment unit can benefit from logical separation as complexity grows, while a single project works well for many applications and separate projects should be added for concrete reasons; the candidate treats layers as a trade-off rather than a mandatory fixed structure.
